value.rationale: Minimal Hamming separation of two distinct predecessors is a natural invariant of reversible-layer-plus-difference cyclic dynamical maps and controls how spatially distant indistinguishable inputs must be. The nonlinear automaton has the same two-predecessor multiplicity as the linear cyclic difference but dramatically smaller optimal separation (asymptotic fraction 1/3 rather than 1), with a nontrivial exact mod-three finite-size obstruction. The result is a natural complete classification for an explicit recently investigated unresolved 2-to-1 rule rather than an arbitrary parameter slice; no broader chaos or cryptographic theorem is claimed.
